question: Which type of amblyopia is most likely to be missed without formal visual acuity testing, because the affected eye appears straight and the child does not squint?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Strabismic amblyopia is associated with a visible squint (manifest deviation), which alerts parents and teachers to seek assessment.

Correct. In anisometropic amblyopia, the inter-eye refractive difference causes suppression of the more ametropic eye — but both eyes may appear aligned and the child uses the better eye without complaint, masking the amblyopia until formal acuity screening is done.

answers.text: Deprivation amblyopia due to unilateral congenital cataract

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Congenital cataract is usually detected clinically as a white pupillary reflex (leukocoria) — it is visible on examination and in flash photographs.

Ametropic (bilateral) amblyopia can also be missed, but the question asks which type is characteristically silent and invisible without VA testing. Anisometropic amblyopia is the classic hidden amblyopia because the eye looks straight.

overallFeedback.feedback: Think about which amblyopia type leaves no external clue. Anisometropic amblyopia has no squint and no opacity — only formal VA testing or refraction reveals the inter-eye asymmetry.
Anisometropic amblyopia is the 'silent thief' — no squint, no cosmetic clue. School vision screening programmes exist precisely to catch this before the critical period closes.
